title: Un- Means Not
objectives: I can tell that un- at the start of a word can mean not.
I can tell that un- on an action word means to undo it.
I can use unlock, untie, unfold, and undo to tell what I do.
I can use unkind and unfair to tell about people and rules.
rationale: Un- is the first prefix first graders can use on their own. Four verbs show un- undoing an action (unlock, untie, unfold, undo) and two adjectives show un- meaning not (unkind, unfair), so children meet both jobs of the prefix and can guess new words such as unwrap or unhappy. Every word is a base the child already knows plus un-. The unit revisits smooth, tumble, and reason, because the same base-word thinking helps with those words and because an unfair rule always needs a reason.

misuse.why: To undo is to take something back. Adding more lines does not take anything back.

words.def: Not right; one person gets more than another.

passage.title: Ben's Birthday Box
paras: Ben got a locked box for his birthday. He used a key to unlock it. Inside, he had to untie a ribbon and unfold a note from Kim. It said, "You were unkind and unfair at recess." Ben felt sad. He wanted to undo it, so he said sorry.

qs.q: How did Ben open the box?
choices: He used a key to unlock it.
He asked Kim to open it.
qs.why: The story says he used a key to unlock the box.

choices: The note said he was unkind and unfair.
qs.why: Kim's note said Ben was unkind and unfair, and then Ben felt sad.

qs.q: What does the word unkind mean in the note?
qs.why: Un- means not, so unkind means not kind or not nice.

write.prompt: Draw something you can unlock, untie, or unfold. Say or write what you do.

parts.m: do the opposite of; undo an action

study.task: Find un- at the start of each word. Cover un- with your finger. What word is left? Tell a partner what un- changes.

groups.label: un- words that undo an action

sentences: Say a sentence about something you unlock at home.
Write a sentence about a time you had to untie something.

combine.model: I used a key to unlock the closed box.
Max had to unfold the paper.

What could we do to undo an unfair rule?

constructed.prompt: Tell how to open a locked box that has a ribbon. Use unlock and untie.
constructed.model: I untie the ribbon first. Then I use the key to unlock the box.

teacher.overview: Children learn that the prefix un- either undoes an action (unlock, untie, unfold, undo) or means not (unkind, unfair). The unit revisits smooth, tumble, and reason.

notes.va.unlock.v: Use a real lock and key or a picture. Ask 'What is the base word?' (lock) and 'What does un- do?'. Pair with lock as opposites.
notes.va.untie.v: Use two laces, one tied and one untied. Children often say untie means not tie; say that it undoes a tie, which reverses it.
notes.va.unfold.v: Fold and unfold a paper in front of the class. Link fold and unfold as a pair.
notes.va.undo.v: Undo has two parts (un + do). Connect to the undo arrow on a computer. A mistake can sometimes be undone and sometimes not.
notes.va.unkind.adj: Un- means not here. Role-play kind and unkind choices in a calm way and focus on how the other person feels. Do not name real children.
notes.va.unfair.adj: Use a game where one team gets more and ask 'Is that fair?'. Ask for a reason, which links to the cause unit.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'The word is unlock. I see un- at the start and lock after it. Lock means to close with a key. Un- means to undo, so unlock means to open with a key. I can do this with untie, unfold, and undo too. Now unkind: un- plus kind means not kind, so it means not nice.'
discuss: What other words start with un- that you know?
Is it unfair when a friend does not share? Why?
misconceptions: Every word that starts with un- has the prefix (under and uncle do not).
Unkind means mean on purpose only.
extend: Children find an un- word in a book and tell what the base word is.
Play 'Opposite Actions': say lock, tie, or fold and children say the un- word and act it out.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit un- the next day with unwrap or unhappy, again at one week, and use the prefix when children read or write. The un- idea returns in later grades with re- and dis-.

wida.oral: Partner A says a base word (lock, tie, fold, kind, fair). Partner B adds un- and says what the new word means.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (abrir con llave, desatar, desdoblar, deshacer, poco amable, injusto) are not reviewed by a native speaker; Spanish uses des- for many un- words, which may be worth teaching as a link.
Un- is shown as two parts (do the opposite of; not) in study.parts; both are the same English prefix, split only to help first graders.
The unkind and unfair examples avoid naming real children, and role-play should stay general.
